title: AppFoundry and CRM
summary: The marketplace, the documented Salesforce and Zendesk embeds, and OAuth migrations that do not invent other CRMs.

lessons.title: AppFoundry is the marketplace, not a feature you assume is installed
lessons.summary: An app is present only after someone installs it into the org.
paras: AppFoundry is Genesys’ marketplace for applications that extend Genesys Cloud. The site is the catalog. An org does not gain screen pop, a workforce add-on, or a bot connector because the listing exists. Someone with the right admin rights installs it, and that install often creates an OAuth client.

This lab cites the marketplace and the product articles it can open. If a CRM is not Salesforce or Zendesk in those articles, the lesson will say “look on AppFoundry” rather than invent a feature list. Listings change. Re-open the listing before you write it into a design.

lessons.title: Genesys Cloud for Salesforce is a documented embed
lessons.summary: Screen pop, click-to-dial, logging, and the assist features that page names.
paras: The About Genesys Cloud for Salesforce article describes the embed: agents work in Salesforce with Genesys capabilities such as screen pop, click-to-dial, and interaction logging. The page also discusses Agent Assist and Agent Copilot in that embed. Those sentences are the feature list this lab will repeat. Anything the page does not say, including a field map for your objects, is your design work.

The embed is not the Salesforce OAuth client-credentials migration. Logging a call and calling a Salesforce API from a data action are two integrations. They can share a vocabulary and still use different credentials. Configure both on purpose.

lessons.title: Salesforce data actions move to OAuth client credentials
lessons.summary: Consumer key, secret, and My Domain URL. The request body of the action stays.
paras: The Salesforce OAuth client-credentials migration guide describes leaving username-password auth. You create a Salesforce OAuth client, and you give Genesys the consumer key, the secret, and the My Domain URL. The guide says the data action’s request body does not have to change for that migration. Read the guide for the clicks. This lesson is the shape, not a second copy of the clicks.

A different article, configure OAuth settings, covers CX Cloud from Genesys and Salesforce OAuth settings. Do not mix that page with the data-action migration and call them one wizard. Two pages, two jobs.

figure.caption: Password auth leaves. Client credentials stay. The action body stays.

lessons.title: Zendesk has its own about page, with a similar embed idea
lessons.summary: Do not copy the Salesforce field list onto Zendesk.
paras: About Genesys Cloud for Zendesk documents an embed in the same family: agents handle Genesys interactions from Zendesk, with the screen-pop and productivity features that page describes. Read that page for the list. This lab will not paste unverified feature parity.

OAuth still applies. A Zendesk app that calls the Platform API is a client with a grant and roles. The Salesforce migration guide is not the Zendesk guide. If you need a Zendesk credential change, open the Zendesk article rather than reusing the My Domain steps.

lessons.title: Dynamics, ServiceNow, and the rest stay on the marketplace
lessons.summary: No invented feature lists for CRMs this lab did not open.
paras: People will ask for Microsoft Dynamics and ServiceNow in the same breath as Salesforce. This lab did not confirm a product article for those embeds while it was written. The honest answer is AppFoundry plus the Developer Center: find the listing, read it, and if you build your own, use OAuth and data actions under the rules you already have.

A custom CRM integration is a client and a set of data actions, not a new routing method. The conversation still queues in Genesys. The CRM stores the record. When the data action times out, the agent still has the call. Draw that failure in Architect.
lessons.uncertainty: This lab did not confirm Dynamics or ServiceNow product articles. Do not treat this page as one.

lessons.title: A CRM failure is not an ACD failure
lessons.summary: Screen pop can die while the queue is healthy.
paras: Agents describe a CRM outage as “Genesys is down” because the panel they look at is the CRM. The topology in this lab splits those links on purpose. Data-action timeouts and embed outages leave the conversation on the agent. Your Architect flow should not wait forever on a data action before it transfers to a queue.
Client-credentials roles must include the division that owns the data action and the queue. A 403 that starts on Monday is often a division move on Friday. Check the pair before you rebuild the flow.

figure.caption: The CRM link can drop. The queue link should not.
